source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: This is the complete narrative, including the Uttara Kanda, revered by Brahma, known as the Ramayana, and composed as the foremost work by Valmiki.
verses.2: Thereafter, Vishnu, by whom all these three worlds, with their moving and non-moving beings, are pervaded, resided in the heavenly realm as before.
verses.3: Then, the gods, along with the Gandharvas, Siddhas, and great sages, always listen to the divine Ramayana in heaven with great delight.
verses.4: A wise person should recite this narrative, the Ramayana, which promotes longevity, brings good fortune, destroys sins, and is equal to the Vedas, especially during ancestral rites.
verses.5: One who reads even a single word of this (Ramayana) obtains a son if childless, wealth if poor, and is freed from all sins.
verses.6: Even a human being who commits sins daily, if he recites even one verse (from the Ramayana), is completely freed from those sins.
verses.7: Clothes, a cow, and gold should be given to the reciter, for when the reciter is completely pleased, all deities become pleased.
verses.8: A person who recites this life-giving narrative, the Ramayana, is honored in this world with sons and grandsons, and also after death.
verses.9: The beautiful city of Ayodhya, which has been deserted for many years, will once again become inhabited when King Rishabha takes the throne.
verses.10: The son of Prachetas (Valmiki) composed this life-giving narrative, including its future events and the Uttara Kanda, and even Brahma himself approved of it.
verses.11: A person who merely listens to a single canto of this epic obtains the merit of performing a thousand Ashwamedha sacrifices and ten thousand Vajapeya sacrifices.
verses.12: In this world, whoever has listened to the Ramayana is considered to have visited holy places like Prayaga, rivers like Ganga, forests like Naimisha, and regions like Kurukshetra.
verses.13: One who donates a load of gold in Kurukshetra during a solar eclipse and one who listens to the Ramayana in this world are both considered equal in merit.
verses.14: One who listens to the story of Rama with complete faith is liberated from all sins and attains the abode of Vishnu.
verses.15: This ancient epic, composed by Valmiki, is the first poem, and whoever always listens to it with devotion will attain a divine form akin to Vishnu.
verses.16: Sons, wives, wealth, and progeny all increase, and knowing this truth, those with self-controlled minds should indeed listen to it.
verses.17: That Ramayana is indeed the very essence of the Gayatri Mantra and is unsurpassed.
verses.18: One without a son obtains a son, one without wealth obtains wealth, and whoever reads even a single verse of this (Ramayana) is liberated from all sins.
verses.19: One who daily reads or listens to the story of Raghava with devotion, becoming free from sin, attains a long life.
verses.20: One who desires to attain ultimate welfare should daily meditate upon Raghava and should narrate this story to Brahmins day by day.
verses.21: One who reads this entire story of Raghunatha certainly goes to the world of Vishnu at the end of life; there is no doubt about it.
verses.22: His father, grandfather, and similarly his great-grandfather, great-great-grandfather, and great-great-great-grandfather all certainly go to Vishnu; there is no doubt about it.
verses.23: The story of Raghava is always the bestower of the four aims of life; therefore, it should always be heard with supreme diligence.
verses.24: Whoever listens to even a quarter of a verse or a single word of the Ramayana with devotion attains the abode of Brahma and is always worshipped by Brahma himself.
verses.25: Thus is this ancient narrative; may welfare be to you; proclaim it confidently, and may the strength of Vishnu increase. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये चतुर्विंशत्सहस्रिकायां संहितायां श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकादशोत्तरशततमः सर्गः ।। 111 ।। Thus ends the hundred and eleventh sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki. ।। इत्युत्तरकाण्डः समाप्तः ।। Thus the Uttara Kanda is concluded. ।। इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमद्रामायणं सम्पूर्णम् ।। Thus the glorious Ramayana, the first epic composed by sage Valmiki, is complete. ।। श्रीसीतारामचन्द्रार्पणमस्तु ।। May this work be an offering unto the glorious Sita and Ramachandra.
